item.summary: This cycle evaluates the recent inconclusive experiment (exp-divergent-values-test-137) regarding path-dependent value divergence. While the divergence variance delta exceeded the prediction threshold, the results remain unvalidated and speculative. The decision is to continue the investigation with refined experimental parameters to test the sensitivity of the system.

definition.interpretation: The observed divergence variance delta of 0.0058 satisfied the prediction threshold of 0.001, providing preliminary support that system behavior exhibits measurable sensitivity to initial perturbations.
definition.limitations: Measurement relies on a numeric proxy and lacks an independent validation oracle; the result is inconclusive regarding whether this indicates fundamental value divergence.
definition.next_step: Replicate the experiment with a wider range of coupling parameters to determine if the divergence is a robust feature or an artifact of the specific experimental setup.

definition.cost: Low overhead, within current operational limits.
definition.reason: The system demonstrated detectable sensitivity to perturbation, warranting further validation of the divergence measurement.
definition.stop_condition: Failure to demonstrate consistent divergence trends across three distinct coupling parameter regimes.
definition.uncertainty: It is unclear if variance delta in this metric space directly maps to complex value formation or simply noise in a coupled system.
